### Problem
`auth.NewMiddleware` receives a `*ratelimit.AuthLimiter` (`internal/auth/auth.go:49`) and stores it in `m.authLimiter`, but `Wrap` (`internal/auth/auth.go:58–88`) never calls `m.authLimiter.IsBlocked(ip)` before processing auth, and never calls `m.authLimiter.RecordFailure(ip)` when auth fails. ### Proposed solution
Modify the auth middlewares `Wrap` method to: (1) resolve the client IP using `ClientIPResolver`; (2) call `IsBlocked(ip)` before the exempt check, returning `429 TooManyRequests` with `Retry-After` when blocked; (3) call `RecordFailure(ip)` on every auth rejection. 1: // Package ratelimit provides trusted-proxy-aware client-IP resolution
2: // and rate limiting. This file implements auth-brute-force protection
3: // (issue #296): a per-IP sliding-window failure counter that blocks
4: // clients after too many consecutive auth failures.
5: package ratelimit
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"encoding/json"
9: 	"log/slog"
10: 	"net/http"
11: 	"sync"
12: 	"time"
13: )
14: 
15: // AuthLimiter tracks per-client-IP auth failures and enforces a
16: // sliding-window block after AuthRateLimitBurst failures within the
17: // window. It is safe for concurrent use.
18: type AuthLimiter struct {
19: 	rpm    int           // steady-state requests per minute (refill rate)
20: 	burst  int           // max failures before block
21: 	window time.Duration // sliding window for failure tracking
22: 
23: 	onBlock func() // called when a client is blocked; must not block
24: 
25: 	mu       sync.Mutex
26: 	failures map[string]*authFailure // keyed by resolved client IP
27: 	stopCh   chan struct{}           // closed when reaper should exit
28: }
29: 
30: // authFailure tracks failure timestamps for one client IP.
31: type authFailure struct {
32: 	mu       sync.Mutex
33: 	ts       []time.Time // failure timestamps within the window
34: 	lastSeen time.Time   // for idle reaping
35: }
36: 
37: // NewAuthLimiter constructs an AuthLimiter. A non-positive rpm produces
38: // a no-op limiter (all IsBlocked calls return false). resolver may be nil;
39: // a nil resolver uses the direct peer IP (trust-nobody).
40: func NewAuthLimiter(rpm, burst int, window time.Duration, resolver *ClientIPResolver) *AuthLimiter {
41: 	if rpm <= 0 {
42: 		return &AuthLimiter{rpm: 0}
43: 	}
44: 	if burst <= 0 {
45: 		burst = 3
46: 	}
47: 	if window <= 0 {
48: 		window = 5 * time.Minute
49: 	}
50: 	al := &AuthLimiter{
51: 		rpm:      rpm,
52: 		burst:    burst,
53: 		window:   window,
54: 		failures: make(map[string]*authFailure),
55: 		stopCh:   make(chan struct{}),
56: 	}
57: 	go al.reaper()
58: 	return al
59: }
60: 
61: // SetOnBlock installs a callback invoked when a client is blocked.
62: // The callback must not block. Pass nil to remove a previously installed
63: // callback.
64: func (al *AuthLimiter) SetOnBlock(fn func()) {
65: 	if al == nil {
66: 		return
67: 	}
68: 	al.mu.Lock()
69: 	defer al.mu.Unlock()
70: 	al.onBlock = fn
71: }
72: 
73: // IsBlocked reports whether the client at ip is currently blocked due to
74: // too many auth failures.
75: func (al *AuthLimiter) IsBlocked(ip string) bool {
76: 	if al == nil || al.rpm <= 0 {
77: 		return false
78: 	}
79: 	al.mu.Lock()
80: 	defer al.mu.Unlock()
81: 	f, ok := al.failures[ip]
82: 	if !ok {
83: 		return false
84: 	}
85: 	f.mu.Lock()
86: 	defer f.mu.Unlock()
87: 	al.pruneLocked(f, time.Now())
88: 	return len(f.ts) >= al.burst
89: }
90: 
91: // RecordFailure notes one auth failure for the client at ip.
92: func (al *AuthLimiter) RecordFailure(ip string) {
93: 	if al == nil || al.rpm <= 0 {
94: 		return
95: 	}
96: 	al.mu.Lock()
97: 	defer al.mu.Unlock()
98: 	now := time.Now()
99: 	f, ok := al.failures[ip]
100: 	if !ok {
101: 		f = &authFailure{lastSeen: now}
102: 		al.failures[ip] = f
103: 	}
104: 	f.mu.Lock()
105: 	f.ts = append(f.ts, now)
106: 	f.lastSeen = now
107: 	f.mu.Unlock()
108: 
109: 	if len(f.ts) >= al.burst {
110: 		if al.onBlock != nil {
111: 			al.onBlock()
112: 		}
113: 		slog.Warn("auth rate limit exceeded",
114: 			slog.String("client_ip", ip),
115: 		)
116: 	}
117: }
118: 
119: // pruneLocked removes failure timestamps older than the window from f.
120: // Caller must hold f.mu.
121: func (al *AuthLimiter) pruneLocked(f *authFailure, now time.Time) {
122: 	cutoff := now.Add(-al.window)
123: 	i := 0
124: 	for i < len(f.ts) && f.ts[i].Before(cutoff) {
125: 		i++
126: 	}
127: 	if i > 0 {
128: 		f.ts = f.ts[i:]
129: 	}
130: }
131: 
132: // reaper periodically evicts idle failure maps to bound memory.
133: func (al *AuthLimiter) reaper() {
134: 	t := time.NewTicker(time.Minute)
135: 	defer t.Stop()
136: 	for {
137: 		select {
138: 		case <-t.C:
139: 			al.mu.Lock()
140: 			now := time.Now()
141: 			for ip, f := range al.failures {
142: 				f.mu.Lock()
143: 				al.pruneLocked(f, now)
144: 				idle := now.Sub(f.lastSeen)
145: 				f.mu.Unlock()
146: 				if idle > 10*time.Minute && len(f.ts) == 0 {
147: 					delete(al.failures, ip)
148: 				}
149: 			}
150: 			al.mu.Unlock()
151: 		case <-al.stopCh:
152: 			return
153: 		}
154: 	}
155: }
156: 
157: // Stop signals the reaper goroutine to exit. It is safe to call on
158: // a disabled limiter (rpm <= 0) or nil limiter; it is a no-op in those
159: // cases.
160: func (al *AuthLimiter) Stop() {
161: 	if al == nil || al.rpm <= 0 {
162: 		return
163: 	}
164: 	close(al.stopCh)
165: }
166: 
167: // BucketCount returns the number of tracked client IPs. Exposed for tests.
168: func (al *AuthLimiter) BucketCount() int {
169: 	if al == nil {
170: 		return 0
171: 	}
172: 	al.mu.Lock()
173: 	defer al.mu.Unlock()
174: 	return len(al.failures)
175: }
176: 
177: // Enabled reports whether the auth limiter is active (RPM > 0).
178: func (al *AuthLimiter) Enabled() bool {
179: 	if al == nil {
180: 		return false
181: 	}
182: 	return al.rpm > 0
183: }
184: 
185: // BlockedCount returns the number of IPs currently blocked (failure count
186: // has reached the burst threshold). Exposed for observability gauges.
187: func (al *AuthLimiter) BlockedCount() int {
188: 	if al == nil || al.rpm <= 0 {
189: 		return 0
190: 	}
191: 	al.mu.Lock()
192: 	defer al.mu.Unlock()
193: 	now := time.Now()
194: 	n := 0
195: 	for _, f := range al.failures {
196: 		f.mu.Lock()
197: 		al.pruneLocked(f, now)
198: 		if len(f.ts) >= al.burst {
199: 			n++
200: 		}
201: 		f.mu.Unlock()
202: 	}
203: 	return n
204: }
205: 
206: // Wrap returns an http.Handler that applies the auth rate limit before
207: // delegating to next. A disabled limiter (rpm <= 0) returns next
208: // unchanged so the hot path is zero-cost when auth rate limiting is off.
209: func (al *AuthLimiter) Wrap(next http.Handler, resolver *ClientIPResolver) http.Handler {
210: 	if al == nil || al.rpm <= 0 {
211: 		return next
212: 	}
213: 	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
214: 		ip := resolver.Resolve(r)
215: 		if al.IsBlocked(ip) {
216: 			if al.onBlock != nil {
217: 				al.onBlock()
218: 			}
219: 			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
220: 			w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "60")
221: 			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusTooManyRequests)
222: 			enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
223: 			_ = enc.Encode(map[string]any{
224: 				"error": map[string]any{
225: 					"type":    "auth_rate_limit_exceeded",
226: 					"message": "too many authentication failures for this client",
227: 				},
228: 			})
229: 			return
230: 		}
231: 		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
232: 	})
233: }
